record.original_question: The Fibonacci sequence is defined by F_1=F_2=1 and F_n=F_{n-1}+F_{n-2} for n greater than 2. A Fibonacci prime is a prime number that appears in this sequence. Are there infinitely many Fibonacci primes?

evidence.quote: The Fibonacci sequence is defined by F_1=F_2=1 and F_n=F_{n-1}+F_{n-2}. A prime number is said to be Fibonacci prime if it appears in the Fibonacci sequence. Are there infinitely many Fibonacci primes?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Define the Fibonacci sequence by $F_1 = F_2 = 1$ and $F_n = F_{n-1} + F_{n-2}$ for all integers $n > 2$. Call a prime number $p$ a Fibonacci prime if $p = F_n$ for some positive integer $n$. Determine whether there exist infinitely many Fibonacci primes.
artifact.status_search_result: It is a well-known long-standing open problem in number theory whether there are infinitely many Fibonacci primes. Only finitely many are known, and no proof of infinitude or finiteness exists.

status_evidence.title: Fibonacci prime - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: It is not known whether there are infinitely many Fibonacci primes.
status_evidence.claim: The infinitude of Fibonacci primes is an open problem.
